chunks: 3905 - Abu al-Rabi' said, and Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said:

Concerning a man who comes to the people of a village after the authority has oppressed them, so they became unable to undertake paying its land-tax, while the village is in their hands, and it is not known whether it belongs to them or whether others have some share in it. So they hand it over to him on condition that he pays its land-tax; then he takes it from them, pays its land-tax, and after that a great amount remains in surplus.
So he عليه السلام said: There is no harm in that, if the condition was agreed upon with them accordingly.

key_terms.السُّلْطَانُ: the ruling authority that imposed hardship on the people
key_terms.الشَّرْطُ: the stipulated contractual condition between the parties
key_terms.الْقَرْيَةُ: the village in question as a taxable property or holding
key_terms.خَرَاجِهَا: the land-tax due on the village
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no legal objection or prohibition
key_terms.يَفْضُلُ: there remains as surplus after payment

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to take over a village's tax burden and keep the surplus by prior agreement?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about taking over the management of a village when its people are unable to meet its kharaj obligations due to oppression by the authority. It permits the arrangement, including the resulting surplus, provided that the agreement and condition were properly established with the people concerned.
